name: Health Systems and AI Vendors
title: Health Systems and AI Vendors
answer: Health systems are signing enterprise agreements with AI vendors for tools covered by business associate agreements. OpenAI's healthcare offering lists deployments at Boston Children's Hospital, Cedars-Sinai, HCA Healthcare and UCSF.

reading.body:
Health systems are signing enterprise AI agreements under business associate agreements, and OpenAI's healthcare offering lists four named deployments: Boston Children's Hospital, Cedars-Sinai, HCA Healthcare and UCSF.

The pattern is procurement, not piloting. These are named institutions, not anonymous early adopters, and the agreements are enterprise-wide rather than departmental trials. That matters because hospital AI runs on the same substrate as everything else in this ecosystem: contracts, governance review, and the compute the vendor supplies. The data does not say what hardware sits behind these deployments or where it runs, so no claim about local power or data center load can be made from it.

The governance detail is the part worth keeping. A business associate agreement covers privacy obligations, not whether patient data trains the vendor's models. Those are separate terms, negotiated separately, and the data gives no indication of what any of these four systems agreed to. A reader should treat the deployment list as evidence that enterprise healthcare adoption is real and named, and treat the training-data question as open at every one of them.

What the data does not cover: contract values, model versions, clinical outcomes, or whether these deployments have scaled past an initial site. It is a vendor's own list of customers, which establishes that the agreements exist and nothing about how they perform.
